name: InVision
tagline: Digital product design and prototyping platform for teams.
description: InVision is a design review and collaboration platform, formerly prototyping-led, with a freemium band of $9.95-100/mo and no simultaneous editing support.

The product's direction is documented rather than assumed: two separate pricing entries record a shift from prototyping toward design review and collaboration
Seven comparison records and four alternative listings place it squarely against Figma, Zeplin, Sketch, Affinity, Framer, and Webflow, so a shortlist builds from this repository alone
The dataset records InVision as cloud-delivered with a recorded API, which suits a review artifact that has to reach more than one person
cons: Simultaneous design editing is recorded as unsupported, so live co-authoring on one canvas is out of scope by our records

Rating records disagree inside the repository: this page carries 4.2 out of 5 while four alternative pages list InVision at 4.3

content.title: From prototyping tool to review tool
content.body: This repository files InVision as a digital product design and prototyping platform for teams, and its own write-ups describe a product that has moved. The design software cost blog records that InVision's pricing evolved significantly as the tool shifted from a prototyping platform to a design review and collaboration tool, and the UI/UX pricing entry repeats the conclusion: pricing that reflects a focus on design review and collaboration. Read together, those records describe a tool whose original job is no longer its center of gravity, which leaves this page describing the review product while the tagline above it still names prototyping.

content.title: The review and feedback ecosystem
content.body: What remains recorded as InVision's center is a review and feedback ecosystem, and the prototyping comparison in this repository is the source for that phrase. It uses the ecosystem as the distinguishing claim rather than a feature list: among four prototyping tools it assigns each one a distinct job, and InVision's is the team that still relies on its review loop. The distinction is about who stays rather than what is newest, which describes a team with an established process around review rather than a team selecting a design tool from scratch. That is a different buying situation, and it is the one this product is recorded as serving.

content.title: The four tools our prototyping comparison names
content.body: One comparison in this repository sets the market this product sits in, and it does so by segment rather than by ranking: each of the four tools is given a different job, which is more useful for a shortlist than a score would be. InVision's entry is the one tied to an existing review process rather than to a design surface, which is also the clearest statement of its recorded position. The segments are:
items: Figma, recorded for cross-functional team collaboration
Sketch, recorded for Mac-native design workflows
Framer, recorded for marketing and landing page prototyping
InVision, recorded for teams that still rely on its review and feedback ecosystem

content.title: What our records say it does not do
content.body: One limitation is stated outright in this repository rather than inferred: the collaboration write-up records that InVision does not support simultaneous design editing. That is a structural boundary rather than a missing toggle — two people cannot work the same canvas at the same moment, so review happens on a shared artifact instead of inside a live one. The shift described in the pricing entries points the same direction, since a tool oriented around review and collaboration is read and commented on more than it is co-authored. A buyer whose requirement is real-time co-editing already has the answer in that single sentence from our records.

content.title: A pricing band that has moved with the product
content.body: This page records InVision as freemium with a band of $9.95-100/mo. That band sits beside a record of change: the cost blog states that pricing evolved significantly during the shift from prototyping to design review, and the UI/UX pricing entry describes pricing that reflects a design review and collaboration focus rather than a prototyping seat. The readings on this page were taken from this repository's stored write-ups — cost guides, comparison pages, and the fields attached to the review — without anyone in this project using the product. The band is the figure our dataset currently holds, and the history around it is the reason it should be confirmed against the vendor's own pricing page.

content.title: Cloud delivery, with certifications off the record
content.body: The dataset records InVision as run from vendor infrastructure with its API interface marked available, which matches a review workflow in which a shared artifact has to be visible to more than one person. What the repository does not store for InVision is any compliance evidence plus wording about support tiers: no attestation accompanies this product, and nothing here states support channels or response commitments. That silence marks a gap in our records rather than a verdict on the product, so it can be used neither to clear nor to fail a security review. Buyers with certification requirements take the question to the vendor and read their published documentation rather than resolving the question from this page.

content.title: InVision next to Figma, Zeplin, and Sketch
content.body: Seven comparison records in this repository pair InVision with another product. The rows place it ahead of Adobe Express, Adobe XD, and Sketch on user rating, and behind Affinity, Canva, Figma, and Zeplin, with starting price marked in its favor against Figma and the other way against Zeplin. This page carries 4.2 out of 5 from 2,360 reviews.

content.title: Who still standardizes on it
content.body: The phrasing in this repository's prototyping comparison is the clearest statement of fit on record: teams that still rely on its review and feedback ecosystem. That describes an installed-base buyer — an organization where designers, product managers, and stakeholders already review work here, and where moving the review habit would cost more than the subscription does. The recorded shift from prototyping toward design review points the same way from the vendor's side. It is a weaker proposition for a team choosing its first design tool, since the comparison records place Figma, Zeplin, and Affinity ahead of InVision on user rating.

content.title: Fit, and the record behind it
content.body: Together the records describe a cloud design review and collaboration product, freemium here at $9.95-100/mo, rated 4.2 out of 5 from 2,360 reviews, and explicitly recorded as not supporting simultaneous design editing. It fits a team whose review process already lives in this tool, and it does not fit a requirement for live co-authoring on a single canvas. Three questions stay open in the dataset: the plan structure behind the band, the certification status the repository does not hold, and the source of the differing rating its alternative pages carry. None of the three resolves from this page.

faqs.question: Is InVision still a prototyping tool?
faqs.answer: The tagline here says prototyping, but two pricing entries record a shift: the product has moved from a prototyping platform to a design review and collaboration tool, and its pricing now reflects that focus.

faqs.question: Can two designers edit the same design at once?
faqs.answer: Not by our records: the collaboration write-up states that InVision does not support simultaneous design editing, so review happens on a shared artifact rather than inside a live canvas.

faqs.question: What price does this page record for InVision?
faqs.answer: A freemium model with a band of $9.95-100/mo, alongside a cost-blog note that pricing evolved significantly while the product shifted toward design review and collaboration.

faqs.question: How does InVision compare with Figma and Zeplin here?
faqs.answer: Seven comparison records place it behind Figma, Zeplin, Affinity, and Canva and ahead of Adobe Express, Adobe XD, and Sketch, with the starting-price row going its way against Figma.

faqs.question: Which alternatives does this repository list for InVision?
faqs.answer: Adobe Express, Adobe XD, Sketch, Affinity, Canva, Figma, and Zeplin are the seven tools this repository pairs it with in its comparison records.

author: Emily Nakamura
learningCurve: Beginner — the first useful output comes within an hour
whoShouldUse: Teams whose design review process already runs through InVision, where designers, product managers, and stakeholders read and comment on work rather than co-authoring a single canvas together.
whoShouldNotUse: Buyers who need simultaneous editing of one design file, or teams choosing a first design tool where this repository's comparison records place Figma, Zeplin, and Affinity ahead on user rating.
